newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Underperform ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Underperform ahead of data.

text.p: Australian bonds underperformed against the dollar as an initial drift up in yields triggered further technical selling.

The move was largely playing catch up after the weak performance seen in U.S. Treasuries while Australian markets were closed for the long holiday weekend, and amid caution ahead of this week's host of data both locally and in the U.S.

However, "Whereas the U.S. market will react to strong data, the Australian market will be increasing vulnerable to weak activity data and benign price data," said Glenn Maguire, economist at Societe Generale.

The domestic market will see average weekly ordinary time earnings on Thursday and retail trade data on Friday, while a steady stream of U.S. data ends the week with the key April non-farm payrolls report.

"It is expected that the employment data in the U.S. will drive U.S. Treasury yields higher. This will keep Australian bonds under pressure, however, decelerating earnings data, with more mixed activity data, could see the spread heading towards the 80 basis point low seen in January," Maguire added.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread got down to the low 90s last week before profit-taking saw this move reversed.

Meanwhile, spread movements were less notable against Canadian debt with the market undermined on Friday by a weakening Canadian dollar. Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien called a general election for June 2 on Sunday.
Elsewhere, the New Zealand market was buoyed by an agressively bid bill market on the continued strength of the N.Z. dollar.
